section_summary: This section documents Japanese rules for foreign aircraft, including approved routes, landing fields, restricted zones, and bans on carrying cameras and weapons. Much of the correspondence concerns whether Japan could require permission for flights over the South Manchuria Railway Zone, a claim the U.S. State Department distinguished from Japan's authority in the Kwantung Leased Territory. Later papers address the investigation of aviators Pangborn and Herndon and the preparation of guidance for American airmen.

people.name: Francis White
people.role: State Department official; Assistant Secretary of State

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. chargé d'affaires ad interim in Japan

people.name: Eugene H. Dooman
people.role: First Secretary of the U.S. Embassy in Japan

people.name: Mark L. Bristol
people.role: Admiral and commander in chief of the U.S. Asiatic Fleet

people.name: Tani
people.role: Chief of the Asia Bureau, Japanese Foreign Office

subfiles.title: Document file note on Ford aircraft flight
subfiles.about: Points to correspondence on Japanese permission for a Ford aircraft flying from Japan to China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Japanese demands concerning flight over the South Manchuria Railway Zone.

subfiles.title: Document file note on Japanese flight instructions
subfiles.about: Indexes Ambassador Forbes's despatch on flight routes and landing fields.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch No. 64 and its attached Japanese instructions.

subfiles.title: Despatch on postponed world flight
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, U.S. Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Japan's requirements for the postponed Marsalis, Williams, and Lundgren world flight.
subfiles.summary: Japan requires a renewed landing application and details of the planned date and any wireless equipment, cameras, or firearms. Forbes forwards route and landing-field instructions.

subfiles.title: Japanese flight route and Kasumigaura field instructions
subfiles.about: Specifies permitted routes over Japan and conditions at Kasumigaura Naval Aviation Field.
subfiles.summary: The instructions prescribe routes from Vladivostok and toward America, prohibit flights over Tokyo and fortified zones, and ban explosives, weapons, ammunition, and cameras. They describe runway lengths and hazards at Kasumigaura.

subfiles.title: Department instruction enclosing Mukden despatch
subfiles.from: Francis White, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests Embassy comment on Japanese requirements for flights over Manchurian railway territory.
subfiles.summary: The Department forwards the Mukden consul general's account of restrictions concerning the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone and asks for the Embassy's views.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on the Hutton flight and Japanese jurisdiction
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, U.S. Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reviews Perry Hutton's flight and the legal basis claimed for Japanese control of the railway zone.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy recounts Hutton's requested route, Japan's refusal to permit a Dairen landing, and the eventual permission to cross the South Manchuria Railway Zone at Mukden. It questions reports that other foreign aviators crossed without consent. Forbes suggests that Japan's administrative position in the railway zone might resemble its position in the Kwantung Leased Territory, while requesting guidance on the distinction.

subfiles.title: Embassy letter to Minister Johnson
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, for the U.S. ambassador
subfiles.about: Seeks evidence and comment on foreign flights over the railway zone.
subfiles.summary: Dooman asks whether foreign aircraft crossed the zone without railway consent and seeks the Legation's view of U.S. recognition of Japanese administrative rights. He also corrects a transmitted phrase in an earlier telegram.

subfiles.title: Letter on the legal status of Kwantung
subfiles.about: Summarizes U.S. precedents concerning jurisdiction in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: Neville cites published diplomatic correspondence on leased Chinese ports, consular jurisdiction, and the transfer of Kwantung from Russian to Japanese control. He concludes that American consuls had no extraterritorial jurisdiction in Dairen, while noting that the cited sources do not directly address naval visits.

subfiles.title: Department response distinguishing the railway zone
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Directs the Embassy to earlier instructions on U.S. citizens in the South Manchuria Railway Zone.
subfiles.summary: Points the Embassy to 1921 instructions bearing on Japanese jurisdiction in the railway zone.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese control of flights over the railway area
subfiles.about: Explains the U.S. distinction between Kwantung and the railway zone and recommends a response to Japanese flight demands.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum assembles prior U.S. correspondence and states that the railway company holds commercial rights, while China retains political jurisdiction and sovereignty over the zone. It suggests practical local notice for flights near railway settlements but advises against seeking Japanese diplomatic permission. It invokes the 1919 Paris Convention's airspace rule to support China's authority over flights.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting Dooman's records and clarification
subfiles.to: U.S. Embassy, Tokyo; Eugene H. Dooman
subfiles.about: Requests official copies of enclosures and clarification of Japan's requested 'understanding' for flights.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether 'understanding' means advance notice alone.

subfiles.title: Solicitor's memorandum on draft telegram
subfiles.about: Comments on the proposed inquiry about Japan's wording.
subfiles.summary: Finds no objection to the telegram and favors the interpretation in Dooman's January 15 memorandum.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on conversations with Tani
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, for the chargé d'affaires
subfiles.about: Reports Tani's explanation of Japanese expectations for flights across the railway zone.
subfiles.summary: Dooman forwards conversation memoranda and a Foreign Office précis of Hutton's case. Tani says Japan seeks advance notification and might suggest deferring a flight, but has not formally required permission to cross the railway zone. Dooman disputes the Japanese secretary's account of what the Embassy was originally told. Page 27 contains a later Department file annotation on this despatch.

subfiles.title: Dooman memorandum of first conversation with Tani
subfiles.about: Records Tani's account of the misunderstanding over Hutton's railway-zone flight.
subfiles.summary: Tani says Japan wants previous intimation, not a formal permission request. Dooman maintains that the Foreign Office secretary had repeatedly used the word 'permission.'

subfiles.title: Dooman memorandum of second conversation with Tani
subfiles.about: Records Tani's renewed assurance that Japan had imposed no formal railway-zone permission rule.
subfiles.summary: Tani acknowledges the earlier misunderstanding and repeats the request for an 'understanding' before flights.

subfiles.title: Foreign Office précis of the Hutton case
subfiles.about: Presents the Foreign Office account of Hutton's requested route and landing rights.
subfiles.summary: The précis distinguishes Japanese permission for Kwantung from an 'understanding' for crossing the railway zone.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch forwarding Japanese flight stipulations
subfiles.about: Forwards three sets of Japanese stipulations for American aviators.
subfiles.summary: Forbes supplies rules for flights arriving from the Pacific, arriving from the Asian continent, and traveling within Japan. He notes the strict limits applied to foreign aviators.

subfiles.title: Stipulations for flights from trans-Pacific points
subfiles.about: Sets the route and restrictions for aircraft approaching Japan across the Pacific.
subfiles.summary: Requires a Kuril Islands–Miyako–Tachikawa route, bans flights over Tokyo and restricted areas, and bars cameras and weapons.

subfiles.title: Stipulations for flights from the Asian continent
subfiles.about: Sets routes, fields, restrictions, and customs conditions for flights entering from the continent.
subfiles.summary: Lists approved routes through Korea and Japan, landing and emergency fields, prohibited cargo, restricted zones, advance arrival notice, and a customs deposit or guarantee.

subfiles.title: Stipulations for flights within Japan
subfiles.about: Prescribes routes and permissions for foreign aircraft making domestic flights.
subfiles.summary: Specifies routes from Tachikawa to Osaka, Fuji, Sendai, and toward Mukden; names landing fields; and requires advance notice or military permission for certain fields. It also restricts Tokyo overflights, cameras, prohibited areas, and paid carriage.

subfiles.title: Copy of Forbes's July 15 despatch
subfiles.about: Duplicates the cover despatch transmitting three sets of Japanese flight rules.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the despatch on routes and restrictions for foreign aviators in Japan.

subfiles.title: Copy of trans-Pacific flight regulations
subfiles.about: Duplicates the rules for aircraft arriving from trans-Pacific points.
subfiles.summary: Copy specifies the approach route, landing field, prohibited areas and cargo, and arrival notice.

subfiles.title: Copy of continental flight regulations
subfiles.about: Duplicates the rules for flights entering Japan from the Asian continent.
subfiles.summary: Copy lists routes and fields, prohibited areas and cargo, and customs conditions.

subfiles.title: Copy of regulations for flights within Japan
subfiles.about: Duplicates the detailed routes and limits for foreign aircraft flying within Japan.
subfiles.summary: The copy lists domestic routes and fields, advance notice and military approval requirements, restricted areas, camera restrictions, and a ban on carrying passengers or freight for pay.

subfiles.title: File note on Pangborn and Herndon's photographs
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram about photographs taken over Japanese fortified zones.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Japanese official displeasure over photographs taken without permission.

subfiles.title: File note on aviation-law infraction
subfiles.about: Cross-references correspondence on an aviator's reported violation of Japanese law.
subfiles.summary: The damaged note refers to a flight-related legal infraction.

subfiles.title: Forbes telegram on Pangborn and Herndon's investigation
subfiles.about: Reports the aviators' permit status, questioning, alleged offenses, and public reaction.
subfiles.summary: Forbes states that the pair had only emergency landing authorization. They face examination over an unauthorized flight, a camera, and overflight of fortified territory; officials expect punishment, while press and public reactions vary.

subfiles.title: File note on detention of Pangborn and Herndon
subfiles.about: Points to inquiries into the aviators' detention for breaking Japanese flight rules.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a telegram about Pangborn and Herndon's detention.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department request for Japanese rules
subfiles.from: Clarence M. Young, Acting Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards a librarian's request for Japanese flight regulations.
subfiles.summary: Asks State to supply the Aeronautical Chamber of Commerce with available information.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Swerig's inquiry
subfiles.from: Francis White, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds to Commerce about V. P. Swerig's request for Japanese flight rules.
subfiles.summary: State reports that the Tokyo Embassy supplied material for Commerce's proposed aviation guidance and suggests sending that information to Swerig.

subfiles.title: Commerce Aeronautics Branch reply to Swerig
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Swerig's request for information on Japanese flight rules.
subfiles.summary: Says the request was referred to State and encloses an Air Commerce Bulletin article.

subfiles.title: Swerig's inquiry about flight regulations
subfiles.about: Asks for rules omitted from published guidance on foreign flights.
subfiles.summary: Requests information on flying regulations in Japan for the chamber's files.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese pilot's license suspension
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram comparing punishment of Japanese and foreign pilots.
subfiles.summary: Notes that a Japanese pilot could lose a license for at least three months.

subfiles.title: Forbes telegram on the Pangborn–Herndon decision
subfiles.about: Reports discussions with Japanese ministers about resolving the aviators' case.
subfiles.summary: The communications minister cites legal issues and the suspension ordinarily imposed on Japanese pilots. He promises to seek an early favorable decision; Forbes has deferred a proposed note.

subfiles.title: File note on despatch concerning Pangborn and Herndon
subfiles.about: Indexes a despatch on the aviators' landing without a proper permit.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to the investigation of their August 6 arrival.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on Pangborn and Herndon's violations
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, for the U.S. ambassador
subfiles.about: Details the pair's flight, questioning, alleged violations, and Japanese and press reactions.
subfiles.summary: The aviators had authorization for an emergency landing but arrived in Tokyo without a regular permit. Officials questioned them over the landing, flights above fortified zones, and carrying and using a camera. The Embassy describes public and press reactions, its request for leniency, and enclosed editorials and diplomatic notes. The outcome was still pending.

subfiles.title: Japanese note authorizing emergency landing
subfiles.from: Kijūrō Shidehara, Japanese minister for foreign affairs
subfiles.about: Permits Pangborn and Herndon an emergency flight or landing under specified conditions.
subfiles.summary: Allows flight or landing only when unexpected circumstances require it, subject to Japanese aviation law, cargo bans, restricted zones, and prompt reporting.

subfiles.title: Embassy note regretting the flight incident
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, for the U.S. ambassador
subfiles.about: Expresses regret and requests help for Pangborn and Herndon.
subfiles.summary: Neville acknowledges the rule violations, promises efforts to prevent recurrence, and asks Shidehara to assist the aviators.

subfiles.title: File note on proposed guidance for American airmen
subfiles.about: Indexes Commerce's proposed publication on foreign flight requirements.
subfiles.summary: Notes a manuscript sent to State for approval and suggestions.

subfiles.title: Department telegram requesting Japanese guidance
subfiles.about: Requests review of proposed short guidance for American aircraft entering Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether the draft warnings about prohibited cargo and restricted overflights need amendment.

subfiles.title: Department telegram on publishing full regulations
subfiles.about: Asks whether Commerce should print the Embassy's three full sets of Japanese rules.
subfiles.summary: Requests a prompt recommendation on publication of the regulations enclosed with despatch No. 274.

subfiles.title: Forbes telegram proposing revised guidance
subfiles.about: Relays Japan's proposed wording and other practical requirements for foreign aircraft.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office calls for separate advance permission, route and landing instructions for each flight, and compliance with restricted-zone and cargo rules. Forbes advises that full publication of case-specific instructions would be of limited use. He adds requirements concerning accurate aircraft specifications, airworthiness certificates, and customs surety.

subfiles.title: Department telegram on American airworthiness certificates
subfiles.about: Asks about Japanese acceptance of American aircraft certificates.
subfiles.summary: Notes that U.S. certificates have been accepted elsewhere despite the United States' position under the 1919 convention.

subfiles.title: State Department recommendations to Commerce
subfiles.from: James Grafton Rogers, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Supplies proposed Japanese requirements for Commerce's aviation publication.
subfiles.summary: State recommends a short list covering advance flight permission, route and landing instructions, restricted zones, prohibited cargo, and customs surety. It also proposes that pilots provide accurate aircraft specifications in requests for entry. Guidance on China remains pending.

subfiles.title: Forbes telegram on Japanese enforcement and certificates
subfiles.about: Confirms acceptance of U.S. airworthiness certificates and warns of strict Japanese permitting.
subfiles.summary: Japan has accepted American certificates through Embassy requests; each flight still requires a separate application and careful review.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment of State's guidance
subfiles.from: Clarence M. Young, Acting Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Acknowledges State's revisions to proposed foreign-flight guidance.
subfiles.summary: Commerce says it will follow State's advice in the publication.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment concerning Swerig
subfiles.from: Clarence M. Young, Acting Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Confirms that Commerce will answer Swerig using the newly supplied Japanese rules.
subfiles.summary: Commerce agrees to transmit the information to Swerig.

subfiles.title: File note on Lindbergh's Kuril Islands flight
subfiles.about: Points to a report of a possible unauthorized Lindbergh overflight in the Kurils.
subfiles.summary: Notes suspicion of an infringement and that no action was taken.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on penalties for foreign aviators
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, U.S. Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards a Japanese memorandum on future flights by penalized foreign aviators.
subfiles.summary: Neville reports that Japan will prohibit or suspend flights over its territory by foreign aviators penalized for infringements. The Foreign Office memorandum is identified as an enclosure but appears beyond this section.
